_comment: Transport-crypto provider ledger. See AGENTS.md §Cryptography Policy.
This file records which TLS/QUIC crypto providers are present in the
resolved dependency graph, why each is there, and who reviewed it.
It exists because the previous control -- a source-text ban on crate names
-- could not see feature-mediated provider selection and, separately, had
never executed (vox-code-audit's scanner dropped every Cargo.toml before
any detector saw it; fixed 2026-09-04). A provider is chosen by a FEATURE on
a shared crate, so the only sound input is the resolved lockfile.

allowed_providers.reason: Explicit workspace pin: Cargo.toml `rustls`/`tokio-rustls` both use features = ["ring"]. Also the provider reqwest 0.12.x selects (rustls-tls -> rustls-tls-webpki-roots -> __rustls-ring). iroh 1.x defaults to tls-ring, so the planned mesh transport adds no new provider.
allowed_providers.planned_removal: Interim only. Once hf-hub 1.0 moves the last reqwest-0.12 consumer to 0.13, every consumer is on 0.13, which selects aws-lc-rs. `ring` is then removed and aws-lc-rs becomes the sole provider. VCS is unaffected: jj-lib and gix already require reqwest 0.13. Tracked by plan Task 0.4 Step 5.

allowed_providers.reason: UNAVOIDABLE while preserving features. reqwest 0.13.x maps rustls-tls to __rustls-aws-lc-rs (the provider default changed between reqwest majors). reqwest 0.13 is required by chromiumoxide 0.9.1 (browser plugin) and by gix-transport 0.57.1 <- gix <- jj-lib 0.42 <- vox-vcs. jj-lib exposes no TLS feature at all (default = ["git"], git = ["dep:gix"]), so this cannot be steered from our manifests. Removing it means dropping the browser plugin or VCS.
allowed_providers.planned_role: Becomes the SOLE provider after plan Task 0.4. iroh supports it via `tls-aws-lc-rs`, so the mesh transport does not force `ring` to stay.

duplicates.reason: hf-hub 0.5.0 requires reqwest ^0.12.2; chromiumoxide 0.9.1 and gix-transport 0.57.1 require ^0.13. Incompatible semver majors, so cargo builds both. This split is the ROOT CAUSE of the two-provider state.
duplicates.resolution: hf-hub 1.0.0 (2026-07-10) moved to reqwest ^0.13 and dropped ureq and native-tls. Upgrading collapses reqwest to one major and is expected to leave aws-lc-rs as the sole provider. It is a real API port -- 1.0 drops ureq, and four call sites use hf_hub::api::sync::Api -- so it is tracked as a plan task, not a version bump.

duplicates.reason: vox-crypto pins 2.x; iroh 1.1 pins >=3.0.0-rc. Two majors coexist by necessity. They cannot share a Rust type, but both round-trip through 32 raw bytes, so one stored seed derives both identities.
duplicates.resolution: Accepted. Bridge via SecretKey::from_bytes; never let iroh generate and persist an independent key.

forbidden_providers.reason: C toolchain dependency; not currently in the graph. Keep it that way.
FIPS variant requires cmake + Go, which the build-toolchain invariant forbids.
Pure-Rust provider, but 0.0.2-alpha, unmaintained since 2024-04, README says do not use in production, and its QUIC HeaderProtectionKey is todo!() -- it panics at runtime under a QUIC stack.

build_toolchain_invariant.requirement: A clean clone builds with only the pinned Rust toolchain, the platform C compiler, and Node+pnpm for the GUI.
build_toolchain_invariant.note: aws-lc-sys >= 0.41 satisfies this on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc via pregenerated bindings and prebuilt NASM objects. Verified empirically on BLAPTOP04 2026-09-04: aws-lc-sys built successfully with neither cmake nor nasm on PATH; its own build log records 'NASM command not found'. The old policy banned crates that 'drag in cmake or nasm' -- that hazard is not real for this crate at this version, which is why the invariant is now stated as a property of the build and checked by a CI image lacking those tools.

_target_state.rationale: Single provider, reached by collapsing reqwest to one major rather than by banning a crate name. Costs no features: HuggingFace keeps working (hf-hub 1.0), VCS keeps working (jj-lib/gix already want reqwest 0.13), and iroh supports aws-lc-rs directly.
_target_state.abort_condition: If removing ring forces jj-lib, gix, or chromiumoxide onto a different reqwest major, or breaks the no-cmake/no-nasm build invariant on any platform, keep both providers and record why here.
